To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the extraction of rat liver and rat ascites cells nuclei by 5% HClO4 gives crude Fl histone which contains in addition to histone Fl a number of nonhistone proteins.
The methionine-containing subfraction of F 1 histone from the rat was isolated by a procedure involving perchloric acid extraction and gel filtration on Sephadex G-75.
the methionine-rich proteins are present in the F1 histone fraction of rat tissues and are not present in F1 histone fractions from other tissues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of a methionine-containing subfraction of F I histone from rat tissue.
the structure and function of the methionine containing subfraction of F I histone.
the isolation and characterization of the methionine-rich subfraction of rat Fl histone, and with the elucidation of its biological function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a methionine-containing subfraction of Fl type histone is present in rat tissues, and may be present in other species, but the amount of methionine in the subfraction is not yet established with certainty.
a methionine-containing histone is present in rat tissues.
the methionine-rich protein of crude F1 histone is probably not a minor lysine- rich histone subfraction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a rat-specific subfraction of Fl histone has been isolated.
the methionine-rich protein is not a histone.
the histone of rat is different from that of calf, cat and chicken in that it contains methionine in one of its lysine-rich histoncs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the methionine containing protein is not a major component of Fl histone, and that its presence is due to contamination of Fl with non-histone protein.
there are two distinct classes of lysine rich histones, and that the methionine rich histones are more closely related to the non-histone class than they are to the lysine-rich histon class.

there is a methionine-containing subfraction of F 1 histone in rat tissues that is not present in the same amount in calf tissues, and that this methionine-containing F1 histone is present in rat ascites cells.
